item.title: Lego Robotics for Elementary Students — Sat Aug 1, 1:00 PM — RecRoom
item.description: LEGO Robotics for Elementary Kids (Grades K–5) LEGO Robotics at Kinetic Minds introduces kids to engineering and beginner coding through hands-on building, testing, and problem-solving using LEGO robotics kits. In this small-group, drop-in friendly workshop, kids work in pairs to build real robots, program simple behaviors, and improve their designs through guided challenges. The focus is on curiosity, experimentation, and learning how things work—there’s no single “right” build and no step-by-step cookie-cutter instructions. Workshops are intentionally capped at a low student-to-instructor ratio to support collaboration, confidence, and meaningful learning. Kids will explore: • Engineering and building with LEGO robotics components • Beginner coding concepts (motors, sensors, cause and effect) • Testing, debugging, and iterating designs • Teamwork, communication, and explaining ideas Details: • 60-minute session • Small-group format • No prior experience required Community Spons

item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Fri Aug 7, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream

item.title: Introduction to Wheel Throwing Pottery NEW — Tue Aug 18, 4:00 PM — Montclair - Offsite
item.description:
Note: This is a paid Adult School class. Click here to register.
Discover the art of working on the potter’s wheel in this hands-on 6-week introductory course. Whether you're a complete beginner or looking to refine basic skills, this class offers a welcoming environment to explore the fundamentals of working with clay on the wheel.
You’ll learn the essential techniques of centering, pulling, shaping, and trimming clay to create functional forms like bowls and cups. As the course progresses, you’ll be introduced to glazing methods and the firing process, transforming your pieces into finished, food-safe ceramics. By the end of the session, you’ll have several unique, handmade pieces to take home and enjoy.
All clay, glaze, firings and tools are included.
For the first class, bring an apron or work clothes, sketchbook, writing implement and your curiosity!
Source: Libcal Bccls 10306

item.title: Family History: Through Historical Research and Genealogy — Thu Aug 27, 6:30 PM — West Orange - Community Room 1
item.description:
Information
A method that takes an investigative approach to the study of family history and genealogy. In this presentation, you will hear from a historian who has 25 years of experience doing investigations on innovative approaches to genealogy and how to think differently. There is a wide range of topics that can be covered in this course, ranging from the foundations of using Ancestry and establishing a family tree to more advanced topics such as overcoming brick walls and delving deeper into historical and genealogical material.
About the presenter
James Calaski completed his undergraduate studies at William Paterson University of New Jersey in 1998. He served with the Glen Rock, New Jersey, Police Department for over twenty years, earning numerous awards and citations. He later earned a Master of Arts in History from William Paterson University of New Jersey in May 2013.
This program will be held in Community Room 1.

item.title: Simple Sitting Meditation (15 minutes) — Wed Jul 29, 11:00 AM
item.description:
The Mindful Stream In these sessions, I will be doing guided meditations where we simply sit and notice what arises.
There is no agenda and no plan for how these sessions unfold. I might start off simply by asking us to notice what is already present. By becoming aware of what’s going on in our heads and in our body.
Then, the meditation may take on a life of its own.
Our job is to simply be present to what arises. We may notice the mind moving and chattering about. Or we may notice that it’s completely silent.
The goal here, if there is one, is to simply let ourselves be as we are.
Source: Meetup: The Mindful Stream
